newsitem.title: USA: Iowa, New Hampshire act to keep early contests.
newsitem.headline: Iowa, New Hampshire act to keep early contests.

text.p: Officials from Iowa and New Hampshire launched a drive Monday to keep other states from edging them out as the first to cast votes in the presidential primary and caucus season every four years.

"It's a clear signal to other states that Iowa and New Hampshire will not be caught flat-footed. We're prepared to do what it takes to preserve our position as first-in-the-nation," Iowa Secretary of State Paul Pate said.

He said he and his New Hampshire counterpart had decided to push for creation of a commission that would lobby party leaders to keep the Iowa and New Hampshire contests as the first in presidential election cycles.
For nearly half a century New Hampshire's primary has been the occasion when voters cast the first direct ballots for candidates seeking their parties' presidential nominations.

Since the 1970s, Iowa had been the first state to hold party caucuses, a more indirect form of voting but one that sometimes provides a test of public sentiment. But last year Louisiana and Alaska held caucuses before Iowa's Feb. 12 contest and there were rumblings from other states.
The publicity and attention, as well as the revenue generated by the candidates and the media covering them, make the early contests valuable to the states involved.

Pate said the commission Iowa and New Hampshire were suggesting would consist of the governors and secretaries of state of both states as well as the Republican and Democratic Party chairs in both states. "It's just formalising what we've done for a long time, to try to make sure the rest of the country respects that we play a very important role."
